subject.gist: Mathieu built with earth and straw to escape mortgage payments, living in a shed through construction and retreating to his parents in winter.

story.text: Mathieu wants time for his own projects instead of twenty years of mortgage payments. He builds a small earth-and-straw house with volunteers, using local materials and shaping it around his love of cooking. One stove cooks dinner, warms the house, heats shower water and dries fruit. Even the hole left by digging plaster earth becomes a greenhouse. Getting here means two years based in a shed, with winter retreats to his parents. Now he grows and forages food, hosts friends and cycles to the train. His advice is to stay near your social network: living off the land need not mean cutting yourself off from people.

50 m² (538 ft²) main house, kept small on purpose
About €15,000 to build the house
Two years living in the shed, then the house

Self-drawn plans; a friend checked the calculations
No loan, no mortgage
No real living expenses; about €200 a month for going out with friends
Off-grid solar electricity, solar hot water, wood heat

€35,000 for a south-facing 4,000 m² plot
A 50 m² [538 ft²] house can be submitted without engineer or architect
Round walls were hard to get approved; local houses are square and street-aligned
Authorities could not call it out of keeping: all materials were extracted on site

features.description: The current house has rounded brown walls, exposed roundwood posts and rafters, and a low sloping roof; historical construction inserts expose the straw infill. features.unknown: A measured plan, structural calculations and hidden connections are not verified by the tour.
